World’s most recognised proficiency test for English, IELTS, is a must for those who wish to study abroad. It is also a yardstick for people who wish to travel to foreign countries for employment opportunities. Casper Academy is the top IELTS training centre in Kochi that provides the best classes. Getting a good IELTS band score is the aim of everyone who attends the IELTS examination. It is accepted in 140 countries. Some of the organizations that require IELTS scores include immigration authorities, top universities, schools, government portals and even other employers.

Is Writing the Toughest Part?

Among the four components of IELTS exam, Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing, the last one is considered as the toughest module. Many students who attempt mock-tests consider writing section to be the most challenging one. Many are clueless about the score they will receive even after the exam. You can receive the best IELTS training in Cochin from Casper, that ensures you receive an in-depth coaching to attend the writing part. On an average, the writing score ranges from band 5 to band 8. But writing module will not be a big deal if you have a realistic plan and stick to it with consistent practice. This can assure you a good score in the section. To attempt any exam, you need to have an idea about the test pattern. Writing section consists of 60 minutes, and comprises two tasks. First task consists of 20 minutes and the second, 40 minutes. You are required to write a short essay and a long essay.

Know What an Examiner Requires

At Casper, you will be trained to give effective answers according to the various sections as our IELTS institute in Ernakulam is notable for the right strategies. Your essay should be structured in such a manner that it should have every component that an examiner looks for. The following are some points to be noted while writing an essay:

  • Include facts and statements in your essay.
  • Make sure that you follow the correct structure of an essay- introduction, content and conclusion.
  • Use the most appropriate vocabulary.
  • Provide ample references. Make it more stronger by giving examples to support your points.
  • The examiner will analyse the depth of your coverage.
  • There should be proper connection among the various paragraphs and it should be logically arranged.
  • You should never deviate from the topic. Make sure that you stick on to the topic throughout your composition.
  • Avoid any grammar mistakes as it is sure to give your essay a bad impression. It is better to use simple sentences with accurate grammar than using complex sentences with incorrect grammar.
  • Take care of punctuations. Add the right punctuations wherever necessary.
  • Provide a striking conclusion that contains solutions to the problem, recommendation, and even remedies, if your topic demands.

We provide the best training for IELTS, Cochin has ever seen. To provide some extra tips for writing task, ensure that your article is readable, and distribute facts in proper order. Let your articles flow naturally and contain a well connected structure.
